guide.summary: Notion documents OAuth 2.0 for integrations that each customer authorizes, with the connection set up in the Developer portal. Access is limited to pages each customer shares, and reads require the read content capability.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for Read titles of pages customers explicitly share with the app. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: OAuth 2.0 authorization for customer workspaces is documented
findings.detail: OAuth integrations follow the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow to connect a customer's workspace. Setup requires client credentials and a redirect URI; marketplace submission or review is not required to start authorization.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connects their own workspace through the app.

evidence.quote: Both scoped OAuth integrations and public integrations use this flow. You can start authorization as soon as you configure the integration’s client credentials and redirect URI; Marketplace submission or review
a user-scoped static token, and OAuth integrations and public integrations use the OAuth 2.0 protocol.

findings.title: Read content capability for page titles and content
findings.detail: Retrieving a page and its block children or markdown requires the connection to have the read content capability. Without it, Notion returns 403. This is the only capability needed for the confirmed read-only use case.
findings.appliesWhen: Reading titles and content of shared pages.

findings.title: Customers must share each page with the connection
findings.detail: After authorization, only the authorizing user can share pages with the connection, and pages must be selected in the page picker. Pages not shared return 404, so the app can only read what customers explicitly share.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer must select the pages to share during authorization.

steps.title: Create the OAuth integration and configure client credentials and redirect URI
steps.detail: In the Notion Developer portal, create an OAuth integration, set the redirect URI under OAuth configuration, and choose the installation scope. Confirm the Read content capability under Configuration > Capabilities. Do not enable write or administration capabilities. Save the client ID and client secret in environment variables, never in source control.

steps.title: Retrieve a shared page title with the customer's access token
steps.detail: Retrieve one page the customer explicitly shared. The title is found under the page's properties object: locate the property whose type is title (its key varies by database schema; for a page whose parent is a page the only property is title). Read that property's title array and join every item's plain_text in order to form the title text. For a shared page that is not in a data source, use the property named title. A 404 means the page is not shared with the connection.
steps.doneWhen: The response returns the page object and the title text is produced by joining plain_text from all title array items, or a 404 is reported as not shared. Boundary check: confirm the token holds only the read content capability and the request log contains only this GET; no create, update or workspace administration calls are made.

evidence.quote: ## GET /v1/pages/{page_id} | Retrieve a page
For a page in a data source, the property values follow that data source’s schema. For a page whose parent is another page, the only property is `title`.
## Errors The connection needs read content capabilities. Missing capabilities return `403`. A missing page or missing access returns `404`.

fields: PAGE_ID is a page the customer explicitly shared, provided by the developer
ACCESS_TOKEN from the token exchange response
title located via the property whose type is title, join all plain_text segments of its title array

steps.title: Read the content of a shared page as markdown
steps.detail: Retrieve the page content as markdown with GET /v1/pages/{page_id}/markdown using markdown_version=v2. Read the $.markdown string from the response. If $.truncated is true, repeat the same endpoint with each entry of $.unknown_block_ids as page_id, following the nested blocks until no unknown IDs remain or a 404/object_not_found is returned for a block the connection cannot access. Report inaccessible or unsupported blocks (bookmarks, embeds, link previews, and other unsupported types appearing as <unknown> tags) explicitly as unread beside the markdown; do not claim the markdown is complete when unknown blocks remain. Only the read content capability is used.
steps.doneWhen: The markdown is read in full, or every truncated, inaccessible, or unsupported block is explicitly reported as unread without claiming completeness. Boundary check: confirm the grant is read content only and the outgoing requests include only GET calls to the markdown endpoint for the shared page and its unknown block IDs, with no create, update, or admin operations.

evidence.quote: Response JSON paths for GET /v1/pages/{page_id}/markdown: $.markdown (string)
When truncation or permissions cause unknown blocks, the `truncated` field is set to `true` and the `unknown_block_ids` array contains the affected block IDs.
* **Unsupported block types**: Certain block types (such as bookmarks, embeds, and link previews) are not yet supported in the markdown format.
